overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: its July 13 quasi-judicial session was held solely to render an adjudicatory decision and was exempt from the definition of meeting. No order issued.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board convened a quasi-judicial session on July 13 that was not accessible to members of the public.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, because this portion of the meeting was not a public meeting within the meaning of the Open Meeting Law, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by excluding members of the public from attending the quasi-judicial session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that before convening the quasi-judicial session, the Board required attendees to leave the virtual meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the quasi-judicial session held by the Board on July 13 was solely to deliberate and render a decision following an adjudicatory proceeding and was therefore exempt from the definition of “meeting.”
